meta.competitionFrequencyPerWeek: varies — championship meets are multi-day (heats + finals), not weekly fixtures
meta.notes: Low-impact, high-volume (elite swimmers cover huge weekly distance and ~2000+ shoulder revolutions per arm per session). Strokes: freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly + individual medley. Energy-system demand varies dramatically by event (50 m vs 1500 m) — model the event via the 'positions' archetypes. The GYM is dryland support: it improves propulsive force, start/turn power and — critically — protects the shoulder; it must never add fatigue that degrades pool technique.

maxStrength.why: Supports start/turn power and propulsive force, but swimming is not max-strength limited — buoyancy reduces the role of absolute land strength; technique + specific force dominate.

relativeStrength.why: Strength-to-mass aids propulsion and start power without adding non-propulsive mass; upper-body pulling strength transfers more than lower-body.

explosivePower.why: Block starts, turns and wall push-offs are decisive (especially in sprint events) — short, maximal power efforts.

reactiveStrength.why: Wall push-off and start involve some stretch-shorten action, but far less than land plyometric sports.

sprintSpeed.why: In-WATER sprint velocity is the performance itself; LAND sprint speed has low direct transfer, so this land quality is rated for its modest relevance.

acceleration.why: Start dive + breakout acceleration off the blocks/walls; brief but important in short events.

deceleration.why: Minimal — no land braking demand; only turn approach control. Low priority.

changeOfDirection.why: Only the turn; no open-water multidirectional COD. Low priority for pool swimming.

aerobicEndurance.why: Training is highly aerobic and most events (200 m+) are aerobically biased; distance events are aerobic-dominant. Event-dependent (lower for 50/100).

anaerobicEndurance.why: 100 m and 200 m races are heavily glycolytic — lactate tolerance is a key determinant of sprint-to-middle performance.

repeatSprintAbility.why: Relevant to high-intensity training sets and relay/heats-finals scheduling; a single race is one effort.

mobility.why: A DEFINING swimming quality: shoulder/thoracic range for the stroke, and ankle plantarflexion range for an effective kick — limited mobility both slows the swimmer and drives shoulder injury.

stability.why: Scapular/shoulder stability and core stability transfer propulsive force and protect the shoulder; instability is a primary injury driver.

rotationalPower.why: Long-axis body roll (freestyle/backstroke) and trunk undulation (fly/breast) generate and transmit force through the trunk.

gripStrength.why: The hand acts as a paddle and forearm 'catch' matters, but grip strength per se is not a limiter.

neckStrength.why: Low demand (breathing rotation aside); no contact. Low priority.

balance.why: Body-position 'balance' in the water is a technique construct; land balance has low relevance.

coordination.why: Stroke technique, bilateral limb timing, breathing rhythm and stroke-to-kick coordination are among the highest skill demands in sport.

energySystems.workToRestRatio: training-set dependent; races are single continuous efforts
energySystems.matchDemands: Highly event-dependent: 50 m ≈ ATP-PC/glycolytic dominant (~10-20% aerobic); 100 m ≈ balanced glycolytic/aerobic (~40% aerobic); 200 m ≈ ~50% aerobic; 400 m ≈ ~70-80% aerobic; 1500 m ≈ ~85-90% aerobic. Values above are a 200 m-representative midpoint.
energySystems.heartRateProfile: Race HR near-maximal; training spans aerobic threshold sets to maximal sprint work.
energySystems.fatigueProfile: Stroke length and technique degrade under fatigue (the swimming-specific failure mode); shoulder force output also declines, raising injury risk late in heavy sets.
energySystems.source: swimming physiology (Maglischo; Pyne); event-specific estimates vary — treat as indicative
energySystems.notes: Because the spectrum is so wide, the engine should read the event archetype (positions) rather than a single split.

movementProfile.jointLoading: High REPETITIVE shoulder load (abduction + internal rotation under load); medial knee valgus stress (breaststroke whip kick); lumbar extension load (butterfly/breaststroke undulation, backstroke).
movementProfile.groundContacts: None (low-impact — a major durability advantage over land sports). Loading occurs at the start block and wall push-offs only.
movementProfile.landingDemands: None in-water; dryland plyometric/landing load is a deliberate added stimulus, dosed carefully.
movementProfile.jumping: Only the block start (an explosive dive) — not repetitive jumping.
movementProfile.rotating: Long-axis body roll (freestyle/backstroke) is continuous; trunk rotation for breathing.
movementProfile.overheadActions: Continuous — the entire stroke is an overhead/elevated arm action (the root of shoulder overuse).
movementProfile.repeatedImpacts: No ground impact, but very high repetitive SHOULDER cycles (the dominant cumulative load).
movementProfile.asymmetricLoading: Unilateral breathing-side preference and single-stroke specialisation create left-right and rotational asymmetries to monitor.
commonDeficiencies: posterior cuff (external rotation) weak relative to internal rotators

common.name: Swimmer's shoulder (subacromial pain / rotator-cuff tendinopathy / instability)
common.incidence: highest by far (the signature swimming injury)
common.mechanism: high-volume overhead loading; supraspinatus tendinopathy from swim volume; scapular dyskinesis + internal>external rotator imbalance; underlying joint laxity
common.rtpConsiderations: Restore scapular control + posterior-cuff strength + thoracic mobility; graded return to yardage; reduce paddle/volume on return.
common.source: Sein 2010 (supraspinatus tendinopathy in elite swimmers); Bak 2010 (review); Kibler (scapular dyskinesis)

common.name: Breaststroker's knee (medial knee pain)
common.mechanism: repetitive valgus + external-rotation load of the whip kick
common.rtpConsiderations: Technique modification, hip strengthening, kick-volume management.

common.name: Low back pain (extension-based)
common.mechanism: repeated lumbar hyperextension in undulation; hyperlordotic posture
common.rtpConsiderations: Core anti-extension training, technique, load management.

injuryProfile.summary: Overwhelmingly OVERUSE injuries (the upside of a no-impact sport). The shoulder is THE target — modifiable via scapular/posterior-cuff strength, mobility and load management. Breaststroker's knee and extension-based low-back are stroke-specific secondary targets.

positions.name: Sprinter (50-100 m)
positions.movementDemands: Maximal power output; explosive start + turns; short maximal swim.
positions.bodyComposition: Powerful, muscular, often taller; higher lean mass than distance swimmers.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Lower aerobic volume — tolerates more dryland power emphasis.

positions.name: Middle-distance (200 m)
positions.role: The most complete event — balanced aerobic + glycolytic.
positions.movementDemands: Sustained high intensity with strong anaerobic component.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: High combined load — balance dryland with pool quality work.

positions.name: Distance (400-1500 m)
positions.movementDemands: Sustained submaximal high output; very high training volume.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Highest shoulder-volume exposure — prioritise prehab + load monitoring.

positions.name: Breaststroke specialist
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Monitor medial-knee load; manage whip-kick volume.

positions.name: Butterfly specialist
positions.role: Butterfly events — highest shoulder + low-back load.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Highest shoulder + lumbar load — strict prehab + technique focus.

positions.name: Individual medley (IM)
positions.movementDemands: Competence + capacity across all stroke demands.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Exposed to every stroke's load — broad prehab coverage.

assessments.name: Shoulder internal/external rotation strength + ratio (HHD)
assessments.purpose: Detect the internal>external imbalance that drives swimmer's shoulder; track ER strength + ER:IR ratio.

assessments.name: Shoulder + thoracic mobility screen (incl. GIRD)
assessments.purpose: Total rotation ROM and glenohumeral internal-rotation deficit; thoracic extension/rotation.

assessments.name: Scapular control / dyskinesis screen
assessments.purpose: Identify scapular dyskinesis associated with shoulder pain.

assessments.name: Countermovement jump (CMJ)
assessments.purpose: Dryland lower-body power (start-performance proxy) + neuromuscular fatigue monitoring.

targets.elite: track trend; correlates with start performance

assessments.name: 7x200 m step test (lactate / critical speed)
assessments.purpose: Aerobic/threshold profiling + individualised training velocities; track aerobic adaptation.

assessments.name: Critical swim speed (CSS)
assessments.purpose: Threshold proxy from two time trials (e.g. 400 m + 50/200 m).

assessments.name: Time trials / race-pace performance
assessments.purpose: Event-specific performance benchmark + start/turn split analysis.

assessments.name: Pull-up / lat-pull strength + core endurance
assessments.purpose: Upper-body pulling strength (propulsion proxy) + trunk endurance.

youth.trainingEmphasis: All-stroke technical literacy, bodyweight + band strength, mobility, scapular control; avoid shoulder overuse and overload.
commonMistakes: heavy bench/press work that worsens shoulder balance

development.trainingEmphasis: Build pulling strength + posterior-cuff base; embed prehab; introduce load monitoring (yardage + shoulder).

senior.trainingEmphasis: Individualised event preparation; maintain dryland power at low fatigue; protect the shoulder; nail the taper.

elite.trainingEmphasis: Data-led individualisation; race + taper modelling; precise shoulder-load management.

masters.trainingEmphasis: Maintain mobility + posterior-cuff strength, manage volume conservatively, longer recovery.

offSeason.primaryObjective: Build aerobic base + dryland strength foundation; restore shoulder health and mobility.
offSeason.trainingEmphasis: High aerobic volume, dryland max strength + hypertrophy where needed, shoulder prehab, mobility.

programming.source: swim S&C: off-season rounds out the NEGLECTED LOWER body (swimming is upper/pull-dominant); in-season is stroke/shoulder-specific

preSeason.primaryObjective: Convert base to race-specific speed/power; build race-pace capacity.
preSeason.trainingEmphasis: Race-pace + threshold sets, dryland power, start/turn work; reduce dryland volume as pool intensity rises.

programming.source: swim S&C: off-season rounds out the NEGLECTED LOWER body (swimming is upper/pull-dominant); in-season is stroke/shoulder-specific

competition.primaryObjective: Maintain qualities; sharpen; execute the taper for peak race performance.
competition.trainingEmphasis: Reduced volume, maintained/raised intensity, race-pace sharpening, low-fatigue dryland power, full prehab.

programming.source: swim S&C: off-season rounds out the NEGLECTED LOWER body (swimming is upper/pull-dominant); in-season is stroke/shoulder-specific

playoffs.primaryObjective: Peak taper for championship meet (heats + finals).
playoffs.trainingEmphasis: Minimal-volume high-intensity sharpening; recovery between heats/finals; CNS priming only.
testingRecommendations: readiness monitoring only — no fatiguing tests

recovery.primaryObjective: Physical and mental recovery; restore the shoulder.
recovery.trainingEmphasis: Low/unstructured activity, mobility, light cross-training; rehab carried shoulder issues.
testingRecommendations: none; medical review of carried shoulder issues

oneMatchPerWeek.pattern: Built around key quality pool sessions; dryland placed to NOT fatigue the shoulder before quality swim or racing.
oneMatchPerWeek.heavyDay: early-week, away from key quality swim sets and start/turn work
oneMatchPerWeek.powerDay: mid-week low-volume power (jumps, start work, med-ball)
oneMatchPerWeek.injuryPreventionDay: shoulder prehab embedded daily; primary strength dose early-week
oneMatchPerWeek.typicalLoadingPattern: Aerobic + dryland early → race-pace mid → sharpen → light pre-race → key session/race.
avoidHeavyLiftingDays: day before a key quality swim session

twoMatchesPerWeek.pattern: Multi-day meet: recovery-first between sessions; no heavy dryland.
twoMatchesPerWeek.powerDay: CNS priming only on race mornings if used
twoMatchesPerWeek.recoveryDay: between heats and finals + after each day
twoMatchesPerWeek.typicalLoadingPattern: Heats → recovery → finals → recovery. Dryland is priming/maintenance only.

tournamentOrCongested.pattern: Championship meet over many days (multiple events/sessions): pure freshness management.
tournamentOrCongested.typicalLoadingPattern: Protect recovery + technique between events; dryland is priming, never development.

limitedValue: heavy barbell bench press (can worsen internal-rotator dominance / shoulder balance — use cautiously, prefer push-ups/landmine)
heavy strict overhead press (impingement risk in an already overhead-loaded athlete)
heavy single-leg land strength (low transfer vs upper body)
gymPhilosophy.singleLegEmphasis: Low-moderate — start/turn push is bilateral; lower-body land strength transfers less than upper-body pulling. Some bilateral jump/hinge for start power.
gymPhilosophy.olympicLiftingSuitability: Optional/advanced — useful for start power if competent, but jumps + med-ball deliver much of it at lower technical/shoulder-fatigue cost.
gymPhilosophy.plyometricEmphasis: Moderate, dosed — low-impact sport, so dryland jumps/throws add a deliberate impact + power stimulus (start/turn); progress off a strength base.
gymPhilosophy.coreTrainingPhilosophy: Anti-extension (streamline + undulation control) and anti-rotation dominate; minimal high-volume flexion. Core transmits force between the upper and lower body in the stroke.
gymPhilosophy.rotationalTraining: Moderate — controlled trunk rotation/anti-rotation supports body roll and force transfer; med-ball rotational throws.
gymPhilosophy.isometricTraining: Useful — shoulder/scapular stability holds, streamline holds, tendon-friendly low-fatigue strength in-season and rehab.
gymPhilosophy.tempoRecommendations: Controlled tempo for prehab/scapular work; explosive concentric intent for start/turn power; avoid grinding fatigue near key sessions.
gymPhilosophy.velocityRecommendations: Power work max-intent + low volume; the shoulder is the limiter, so prioritise quality and recovery over dryland volume.

exercises.name: Cable straight-arm pulldown
exercises.primaryAdaptation: lat strength specific to the pull-through

riskFactors: tight hip flexors / limited thoracic mobility
monitoringRecommendations: low-back soreness check in fly/breast specialists

decisionRules.if: athlete reports shoulder pain/soreness OR ER strength drop >15% vs baseline
decisionRules.then: reduce overhead pulling volume + heavy/overhead dryland; switch to pain-free scapular + ER prehab; flag for review; reduce paddles in the pool
remove high-soreness dryland (heavy strength, novel plyometrics, high-volume eccentric); allow only low-fatigue priming
dryland is CNS priming only (a few jumps/throws) or none; no strength development

decisionRules.if: a key quality swim session or start/turn session is scheduled within 24 hours
decisionRules.then: avoid heavy/high-volume upper-body dryland the day before (preserve shoulder freshness for the pool)
reduce whip-kick volume; emphasise hip strength + technique; avoid deep loaded valgus dryland
cap volume/paddle exposure this week; do not add dryland upper volume; monitor shoulder daily
decisionRules.source: Gabbett 2016 (contested — Impellizzeri/Lolli); applied to swim volume

decisionRules.if: readiness score low (poor sleep + high soreness + low wellness)
decisionRules.then: autoregulate down one step; prioritise technique + recovery; do not test
treat as neuromuscular fatigue: reduce CNS/dryland-power load, emphasise recovery, recheck

decisionRules.if: athlete reports systemic illness (fever / below-neck symptoms)
decisionRules.then: withhold training until symptom-free; resume gradually

decisionRules.if: in taper phase before a target meet
decisionRules.then: reduce TOTAL volume substantially (~40-60%) over ~2-3 weeks while MAINTAINING intensity; keep low-volume dryland power; maximise recovery
decisionRules.source: Mujika & Padilla; Bosquet 2007 (taper meta-analysis — much swimming-derived)

decisionRules.then: hold dryland strength/power at minimal effective volume (low volume, high quality, away from key swims); maintain shoulder prehab

acwr.model: acute (7-day) : chronic (28-day) of swim volume (distance) and/or shoulder-load proxy; rolling/EWMA preferred
acwr.source: Gabbett 2016 applied to swim/shoulder load — methodology contested (Impellizzeri 2020, Lolli 2019); soft monitoring input

loadManagement.weeklyProgressionGuideline: Avoid >~10-15% week-to-week spikes in swim volume or paddle exposure; the shoulder is the load-limited tissue.

gymVolumeRanges.inSeason: low maintenance (1-2 sessions; low volume, high quality) + daily prehab

loadManagement.minimumEffectiveVolume: ~1-2 low-volume dryland sessions/week sustains strength/power in-season; shoulder prehab should NOT drop below a daily low dose.
loadManagement.maximumAdaptiveVolume: Off-season — build dryland strength + aerobic base here.
loadManagement.maximumRecoverableVolume: Constrained by total swim volume + SHOULDER tolerance; dryland must never compromise pool technique or shoulder health — total shoulder load is the binding ceiling.
loadManagement.deloadRecommendations: Planned deload every 3-5 weeks in development phases; auto-deload on shoulder-soreness flags, CMJ drop, or volume ACWR >1.5. The taper is a planned, performance-oriented deload.
loadManagement.progressionRules: Progress dryland when quality met at target RPE and shoulder is symptom-free; prefer intensity over volume in-season.
loadManagement.regressionRules: On shoulder flags or red readiness, drop dryland volume first; never schedule heavy upper-body dryland the day before key pool quality work or racing.
loadManagement.missedSessionRules: Do not stack missed dryland; resume at planned level. After time off (esp. shoulder), rebuild yardage + paddle exposure gradually.
loadManagement.source: Mujika/Bosquet (taper); Gabbett (load — contested); Rønnestad (maintenance); expert consensus

thresholds.when: shoulder pain on entry/pull or ER strength drop
thresholds.modifier: cut overhead pulling + heavy dryland upper; prehab only; reduce paddles
treat as accumulating fatigue; ease load

readinessModel.notes: Shoulder soreness is elevated to a top-weight, swimming-specific readiness input. Subjective wellness + sleep + prior load carry the most general weight; objective vitals (HRV/RHR) are trend signals. Raw vitals stay private to the athlete; a coach sees only the derived readiness score (see TEAM-ARCHITECTURE.md).

coachDashboard.principle: Coach sees DERIVED and availability signals only — never an individual's raw HRV/sleep/resting-HR. Aggregated, plain-English, action-oriented.
weeklyReports: swim volume vs plan (squad + per group)
coachDashboard.trafficLightIndicators: Per-swimmer green/amber/red from the derived readiness + load state (no underlying numbers shown).
coachDashboard.privacyNote: All per-athlete entries here are DERIVED (readiness score, load_state, ACWR, adherence %, injury availability). Raw vitals are excluded by design and enforced by the schema validator.

educationTips: why external-rotation/scapular work protects your shoulder
why the taper works (less volume, keep intensity)
why heavy bench can hurt shoulder balance
what your readiness colour means today

strongEvidence: the taper improves performance — reduce volume, maintain intensity (Mujika/Padilla; Bosquet 2007 meta-analysis)
swim volume drives supraspinatus tendinopathy / swimmer's shoulder (Sein 2010)
subjective wellness is a sensitive readiness measure (Saw 2016)
in-season strength can be maintained at low volume (Rønnestad)
weakEvidence: exact ACWR thresholds applied to swim/shoulder load (contested)
scapular/ER programmes reducing injury INCIDENCE (mechanistically strong, RCT evidence modest)
CMJ as a precise start-performance predictor
areasRequiringExpertJudgement: dryland prescription that builds force WITHOUT worsening shoulder balance (bench-press caution)
areasRequiringFutureResearch: shoulder-load monitoring thresholds specific to swimming
long-term shoulder health of high-volume programmes
potentialRisksIfMisimplemented: adding dryland upper-body volume that overloads an already shoulder-loaded athlete
treating ACWR as a hard rule
exposing raw vitals to coaches (privacy + trust breach)
botched taper (too little/too much volume reduction) costing peak performance

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Readiness

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Weekly consistency
athleteDashboardKpis.why: Rewards showing up across a high-frequency programme; consistency beats occasional perfect weeks.

athleteDashboardKpis.why: Race-time improvement is the outcome the swimmer cares about most.

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Shoulder resilience

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Start/turn power

performanceScore.philosophy: Reflects progress toward the demands of competitive swimming, weighted to event-relevant qualities, rewarding consistency and (shoulder) availability and penalising excessive fatigue/poor recovery — never rewarding unsafe shoulder loading.

components.rationale: Consistency drives adaptation across a high-frequency programme.
Shoulder-healthy availability is the strongest performance lever in swimming.
Event time / CSS is the core performance outcome.
Start/turn power is a controllable, decisive margin.
Shoulder/ankle range is both performance and protection — a genuine swimming target.
Dryland pulling strength underpins propulsion + power.
Penalises chronic fatigue/poor recovery; keeps the score sustainable.

guardrails: never increases for training through shoulder pain, red readiness or injury
consistency + availability dominate so the score can't be gamed by occasional max efforts
fatigue/recovery caps the score when recovery is poor
performanceScore.explainability: Each component is shown with its contribution so the swimmer sees why the score moved and what to work on next.

gamification.name: Shoulder-healthy weeks
gamification.rewards: Consecutive weeks available + completing shoulder prehab — motivation tied to the sport's key injury.

gamification.name: Consistency streak
gamification.rewards: Unbroken weeks hitting prescribed pool + dryland sessions; rewards process over outcome.

gamification.name: Prehab badge
gamification.rewards: Completing the shoulder/scapular programme each week — makes the unglamorous work visible.

gamification.name: Mobility milestone
gamification.rewards: Reaching/maintaining shoulder + ankle ROM targets — a swimming-specific development goal.

gamification.name: Testing-battery completion
gamification.rewards: Completing each testing block (ER strength/ROM/CMJ/step test) — encourages objective tracking.

gamification.name: Personal-best milestones
gamification.rewards: Race-time + dryland PRs vs the swimmer's own baseline — self-referenced, not leaderboard.

gamification.name: Long-term development arc
gamification.rewards: Season-over-season time + capability growth — frames the long game over short-term yardage grinding.
